faq.q: What does the cell wall do?
faq.a: The cell wall is a strong layer of cellulose around the membrane. It supports the cell, stops it bursting when it fills with water, and the walls of many cells together hold the plant up.
The nucleus holds the cell's DNA, the instructions for building and running it. It controls which proteins the cell makes.

faq.q: Why do plant cells have chloroplasts?
faq.a: Chloroplasts make the plant's food by photosynthesis, using chlorophyll to trap light energy. Root cells underground have no chloroplasts, because there is no light there.
asks: Do all plant cells have chloroplasts?

faq.a: The large vacuole stores water, sugars and waste in a liquid called cell sap. When it is full it keeps the cell firm; when it shrinks, the plant wilts.

faq.q: How is a plant cell different from an animal cell?
faq.a: Plant cells have a cell wall, a large permanent vacuole and, in green parts, chloroplasts. Animal cells have none of these, but both have a nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria.

facts: Plant cell walls are made mainly of cellulose, the most abundant natural polymer on Earth.
Robert Hooke named cells in 1665 after looking at thin slices of cork under a microscope.
Root cells have no chloroplasts because they grow in the dark.

quiz.say: Which part does a plant cell have that an animal cell does not?
quiz.show: Which part does a plant cell have that an animal cell does not?
quiz.why: Only plant cells (and some microbes) have a stiff cellulose cell wall.
